mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotone climb in RETAIL_REC from -16.3 to -12.0, mirrored by a 7.7-point TRANSIT recovery from -53.3 to -45.6, marks a durable reopening drift; because both series rose together without reversal, the same drift carries retail footfall higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose every week from -16.3 to -12.0
fact:TRANSIT rose 7.7 points over the same window
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below the trailing four-week mean of -13.75 while TRANSIT keeps rising.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 7.9 to 5.7, meaning households are shifting activity out of the home; a further drop below 5.0 is the observable signature of that shift accelerating, which mechanically adds discretionary trips and raises RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 7.9 to 5.7 while RETAIL_REC rose
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0, RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the following week in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery and the WORKPLACES rebound from -20.6 to -13.7 act jointly: resumed commuting simultaneously restores office attendance and generates en-route retail stops, so the combined move lifts RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean above -48 and WORKPLACES above -15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES jumped 6.9 points in the final week to -13.7
fact:TRANSIT reached its four-week high of -45.6 in the same week
failure_condition: Weeks meeting the joint TRANSIT/WORKPLACES condition produce mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days no higher than weeks meeting neither condition.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July heat and the onset of summer holidays push residents toward outdoor leisure; with PARKS holding near -28 instead of collapsing, outdoor activity is not substituting away from commerce and spills into retail-and-recreation spending over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stands at -27.7, 4.7 points above its t-3w value of -32.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above -35 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: Under a de-escalation regime, TRANSIT crossing back above -48 reflects restored capacity limits on shops and venues, so the transit series is the policy channel itself; continued crossing above that level predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -48 and stays there
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -53.3 to -45.6, crossing -48 in the final week
failure_condition: In de-escalation weeks with TRANSIT above -48, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed from 1.3 to 4.7 while RETAIL_REC stayed 12 points below baseline, the signature of precautionary restocking that crowds out discretionary trips; grocery gains crossing 6.0 therefore precede lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 3.4 points across the four weeks
failure_condition: Weeks in which GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 6.0 are followed by RETAIL_REC gains in more than half of cases.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES swung 6.9 points in one week from -20.6 to -13.7; a sustained crossing above -15 confirms a return-to-office regime, restoring weekday commuter footfall around retail premises and lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean stays above -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -20.6 to -13.7 in the final week
failure_condition: Two consecutive weeks with WORKPLACES above -15 are followed by a 14-day mean RETAIL_REC no higher than the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In the summer regime the PARKS-RESIDENTIAL pair matters jointly: falling RESIDENTIAL combined with PARKS holding above -30 means leisure time is spent outside the home and monetised in retail venues, so the joint movement raises RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL below 6.5 and PARKS above -30 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 5.7 while PARKS held at -27.7
regime_hint: summer holiday season with heat-driven outdoor activity
failure_condition: Weeks meeting the joint PARKS/RESIDENTIAL condition show mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days lower than weeks meeting neither condition.
